1.5: The sonnes of Japheth were Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
1.6: And the sonnes of Gomer, Ashchenaz, and Iphath and Togarmah.
1.7: Also the sonnes of Javan, Elishah and Tarshishah, Kittim, and Dodanim.
1.8: The sonnes of Ham were Cush, and Mizraim, Put and Canaan.
1.9: And the sonnes of Cush, Siba and Havilah, and Sabta, and Raamah, and Sabtecha. Also the sonnes of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
1.10: And Cush begat Nimrod, who began to be mightie in the earth.
1.11: And Mizraim begat Ludim and Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim:
1.12: Pathrusim also, and Casluhim, of whom came the Philistims, and Caphtorim.
1.13: Also Canaan begat Zidon his first borne, and Heth,
1.14: And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,
1.15: And the Hiuuite, and the Arkite, and the Simite,
1.16: And the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite.
1.17: The sonnes of Shem were Elam and Asshur, and Arpachshad, and Lud, and Aram, and Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Meshech.
1.18: Also Arpachshad begat Shelah, and Shelah begat Eber.
1.19: Unto Eber also were borne two sonnes: the name of the one was Peleg: for in his dayes was ye earth deuided: and his brothers name was Joktan.
1.20: Then Joktan begat Almodad and Sheleph, and Hazermaueth and Jerah,
1.21: And Hadoram and Uzal and Diklah,
1.22: And Ebal, and Abimael, and Sheba,
1.23: And Ophir, and Havilah and Jobab: all these were the sonnes of Joktan.
1.28: The sonnes of Abraham were Izhak, and Ishmael.
1.29: These are their generations. The eldest sonne of Ishmael was Nebaioth, and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
1.30: Mishma, and Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema,
1.31: Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah: these are the sonnes of Ishmael.
1.32: And Keturah Abrahams concubine bare sonnes, Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah: and the sonnes of Jokshan, Sheba, and Dedan.
1.33: And the sonnes of Midian were Ephah, and Ephar, and Henoch, and Abida, and Eldaah: All these are the sonnes of Keturah.
1.34: And Abraham begat Izhak: the sonnes of Izhak, Esau, and Israel.
1.35: The sonnes of Esau were Eliphaz, Reuel, and Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah.
1.36: The sonnes of Eliphaz, Teman, and Omar, Zephi, and Gatam, Kenaz, and Timna, and Amalek.
1.37: The sonnes of Reuel, Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah.
1.38: And the sonnes of Seir, Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah, and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan.
1.39: And the sonnes of Lotan, Hori, and Homam, and Timna Lotans sister.
1.40: The sonnes of Shobal were Alian, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. And the sonnes of Zibeon, Aiah and Anah.
1.41: The sonne of Anah was Dishon. And the sonnes of Dishon, Amran, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
1.42: The sonnes of Ezer were Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Jaakan. The sonnes of Dishon were Uz, and Aran.
1.43: And these were the Kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before a King reigned over the children of Israel, to wit, Bela the sonne of Beor, and the name of his citie was Dinhabah.
1.44: Then Bela died, and Jobab the sonne of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.
1.45: And whe Jobab was dead, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead.
1.46: And when Husham was dead, Hadad the sonne of Bedad which smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead, and the name of his citie was Avith.
1.47: So Hadad dyed, and Samlah of Mashrecah reigned in his stead.
1.48: And Samlah dyed, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead.
1.49: And when Shaul was dead, Baal-hanan the sonne of Achbor reigned in his stead.
1.50: And Baal-hanan dyed, and Hadad reigned in his stead, and the name of his citie was Pai, and his wives name Mehetabel the daughter of Matred the daughter of Mezahab.
1.51: Hadad dyed also, and there were dukes in Edom, duke Timna, duke Aliah, duke Jetheth,
1.52: Duke Aholibamah, duke Elah, duke Pinon,
1.53: Duke Kenaz, duke Teman, duke Mibzar,
1.54: Duke Magdiel, duke Iram: these were the dukes of Edom.

2.1: These are the sonnes of Israel, Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah, Isshachar, and Zebulun,
2.2: Dan, Joseph, and Beniamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
2.3: The sonnes of Judah, Er, and Onan, and Shelah. these three were borne to him of ye daughter of Shua the Canaanite: but Er the eldest sonne of Judah was evil in the sight of the Lord, and he slew him.
2.4: And Thamar his daughter in law bare him Pharez, and Zerah: so al the sonnes of Judah were five.
2.5: The sonnes of Pharez, Hezron and Hamul.
2.6: The sonnes also of Zerah were Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara, which were five in all.
2.7: And the sonne of Carmi, Achar that troubled Israel, transgressing in the thing excommunicate.
2.8: The sonne also of Ethan, Azariah.
2.9: And the sonnes of Hezron that were borne unto him, Jerahmeel, and Ram and Chelubai.
2.10: And Ram begat Aminadab, and Aminadab begat Nahshon prince of the children of Judah,
2.11: And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz,
2.12: And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Ishai,
2.13: And Ishai begat his eldest sonne Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimma the third,
2.14: Nathaneel the fourth, Raddai the fift,
2.15: Ozem the sixt, and David the seventh.
2.16: Whose sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. And the sonnes of Zeruiah, Abishai, and Joab, and Asahel.
2.17: And Abigail bare Amasa: and the father of Amasa was Jether an Ishmeelite.
2.18: And Caleb the sonne of Hezron begat Jerioth of Azubah his wife, and her sonnes are these, Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon.
2.19: And when Azubah was dead, Caleb took unto him Ephrath, which bare him Hur.
2.20: And Hur begat Uri, and Uri begat Bezaleel.
2.21: And afterward came Hezron to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, and took her when hee was threescore yere old, and she bare him Segub.
2.22: And Segub begat Jair, which had three and twentie cities in the land of Gilead.
2.23: And Gesthur with Aram took the townes of Jair from them, and Kenath and the townes thereof, even threescore cities. All these were the sonnes of Machir the father of Gilead.
2.24: And after that Hezron was dead at Caleb Ephratah, then Abiah Hezrons wife bare him also Ashur the father of Tekoa.
2.25: And ye sonnes of Jerahmeel the eldest son of Hezron were Ram the eldest, then Bunah, and Oren and Ozen and Ahiiah.
2.26: Also Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah, which was the mother of Onam.
2.27: And the sonnes of Ram the eldest sonne of Jerahmeel were Maaz, and Jamin and Ekar.
2.28: And the sonnes of Onam were Shammai and Jada. And the sonnes of Shammai, Nadab and Abishur.
2.29: And the name of the wife of Abishur was called Abiahil, and she bare him Ahban and Molid.
2.30: The sonnes also of Nadab were Seled and Appaim: but Seled died without children.
2.31: And the sonne of Appaim was Ishi, and the sonne of Ishi, Sheshan, and the sonne of Sheshan, Ahlai.
2.32: And the sonnes of Jada the brother of Shammai were Jether and Jonathan: but Jether dyed without children.
2.33: And the sonnes of Jonathan were Peleth and Zaza. These were the sonnes of Jerahmeel.
2.34: And Sheshan had no sonnes, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant that was an Egyptian named Jarha.
2.35: And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife, and she bare him Attai.
2.36: And Attai begat Nathan, and Nathan begat Zabad,
2.37: And Zabad begat Ephlal, and Ephlal begat Obed,
2.38: And Obed begat Jehu, and Jehu begat Azariah,
2.39: And Azariah begat Helez, and Helez begat Eleasah,
2.40: And Eleasah begat Sisamai, and Sisamai begat Shallum,
2.41: And Shallum begat Jekamiah, and Jekamiah begat Elishama.
2.42: Also the sonnes of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel, were Mesha his eldest sonne, which was the father of Ziph: and the sonnes of Mareshah the father of Hebron.
2.43: And the sonnes of Hebron were Korah and Tappuah, and Rekem and Shema.
2.44: And Shema begat Raham the father of Jorkoam: and Rekem begat Shammai.
2.45: The sonne also of Shammai was Maon: and Maon was the father of Beth-zur.
2.46: And Ephah a concubine of Caleb bare Haran and Moza, and Gazez: Haran also begat Gazez.
2.47: The sonnes of Jahdai were Regem, and Jotham, and Geshan, and Pelet, and Ephah, and Shaaph.
2.48: Calebs concubine Maachah bare Sheber and Tirhanah.
2.49: She bare also Shaaph, the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah, and the father of Gibea. And Achsah was Calebs daughter.
2.50: These were the sonnes of Caleb the son of Hur the eldest sonne of Ephrathah, Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim.
2.51: Salma the father of Beth-lehem, and Hareph the father of Beth-gader.
2.52: And Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim had sonnes, and he was the overseer of half Hammenoth.
2.53: And the families of Kiriath-jearim were the Ithrites, and the Puthites, and the Shumathites, and ye Mishraites of them came the Zareathites, and the Eshtaulites.
2.54: The sonnes of Salma of Beth-lehem, and the Netophathite, the crownes of the house of Joab, and half the Manahthites and the Zorites.
2.55: And the families of the Scribes dwelling at Jabez, the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, the Shuchathites, which are the Kenites, that came of Hammath the father of the house of Rechab.

3.1: These also were the sonnes of David which were borne unto him in Hebron: the eldest Amnon of Ahinoam, the Izraelitesse: the second Daniel of Abigail the Carmelitess:
3.2: The third Absalom the sonne of Maachah daughter of Talmai King of Geshur: the fourth Adoniiah the sonne of Haggith:
3.3: The fift Shepatiah of Abital: ye sixt Ithream by Eglah his wife.
3.4: These six were borne unto him in Hebron: and there hee reigned seven yeere and six moneths: and in Jerusalem he reigned three and thirtie yeere.
3.5: And these four were borne unto him in Jerusalem, Shimea, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Salomon of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel:
3.6: Ibhar also, and Elishama, and Eliphalet,
3.7: And Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
3.8: And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine in nomber.
3.9: These are all the sonnes of David, besides the sonnes of the concubines, and Thamar their sister.
3.10: And Salomons sonne was Rehoboam, whose sonne was Abiah, and Asa his sonne, and Jehoshaphat his sonne,
3.11: And Joram his sonne, and Ahaziah his sonne, and Joash his sonne,
3.12: And Amaziah his sonne, and Azariah his sonne, and Jotham his sonne,
3.13: And Ahaz his sonne, and Hezekiah his sonne, and Manasseh his sonne,
3.14: And Amon his sonne, and Josiah his sonne.
3.15: And of the sonnes of Josiah, the eldest was Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, and the fourth Shallum.
3.16: And the sonnes of Jehoiakim were Jeconiah his sonne, and Zedekiah his sonne.
3.17: And the sonnes of Jeconiah, Assir and Shealtiel his sonne:
3.18: Malchiram also and Pedaiah, and Shenazar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
3.19: And the sonnes of Pedaiah were Zerubbabel, and Shimei: and the sonnes of Zerubbabel were Meshullam, and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister,
3.20: And Hashubah, and Ohel, and Berechiah, and Hazadiah, and Iushabheshed, five in nomber.
3.21: And the sonnes of Hananiah were Pelatiah, and Jesaiah: the sonnes of Rephaiah, the sonnes of Arnan, the sonnes of Obadiah, the sonnes of Shechaniah.
3.22: And the sonne of Shechaniah was Shemaiah: and the sonnes of Shemaiah were Hattush and Igeal, and Bariah, and Neariah, and Shaphat, six.
3.23: And the sonnes of Neariah were Elioenai, and Hezekiiah, and Azrikam, three.
3.24: And the sonnes of Elioenai were Hodaiah, and Eliashib, and Pelaiah, and Akkub, and Johanan, and Delaiah, and Anani, seven.

4.1: The sonnes of Judah were Pharez, Hezron, and Carmi, and Hur, and Shobal.
4.2: And Reaiah the sonne of Shobal begat Jahath, and Jahath begat Ahumai, and Lahad: these are the families of the Zoreathites.
4.3: And these were of the father of Etam, Izreel, and Ishma and Idbash: and the name of their sister was Hazelelponi.
4.4: And Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah: these are the sonnes of Hur the eldest sonne of Ephratah, the father of Beth-lehem.
4.5: But Asher the father of Tekoa had two wives, Heleah, and Naarah.
4.6: And Naarah bare him Ahuzam, and Hepher, and Temeni and Haashtari: these were the sonnes of Naarah.
4.7: And the sonnes of Heleah were Zereth, Iezohar and Ethnan.
4.8: Also Coz begat Anub, and Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the sonne of Harum.
4.9: But Jabez was more honourable then his brethren: and his mother called his name Jabez, saying, Because I bare him in sorowe.
4.10: And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, If thou wilt bless me in deed, and enlarge my coastes, and if thine hand be with me, and thou wilt cause me to be delivered from evil, that I be not hurt. And God graunted the thing that he asked.
4.11: And Chelub the brother of Shuah begat Mehir, which was the father of Eshton.
4.12: And Eshton begat Beth-rapha, and Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of the citie of Nahash: these are the men of Rechah.
4.13: And the sonnes of Kenaz were Othniel and Zeraiah, and the sonne of Othniel, Hathath.
4.14: And Meonothai begat Ophrah. And Seraiah begat Joab the father of the valley of craftesmen: for they were craftesmen.
4.15: And the sonnes of Caleb the sonne of Jephunneh were Iru, Elah, and Naam. And the sonne of Elah was Kenaz.
4.16: And the sonnes of Iehaleel were Ziph, and Ziphah, Tiria, and Asareel.
4.17: And the sonnes of Ezrah were Jether and Mered, and Epher, and Jalon, and he begat Miriam, and Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.
4.18: Also his wife Iehudiiah bare Jered the father of Gedor, and Heber the father of Socho, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah: and these are the sonnes of Bithiah ye daughter of Pharaoh which Mered took.
4.19: And the sonnes of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham the father of Keilah were the Garmites, and Eshtemoa the Maachathite.
4.20: And the sonnes of Shimon were Amnon and Rinnah, Ben-hanam and Tilon. And the sonnes of Ishi were Zoheth, and Benzoheth.
4.21: The sonnes of Shelah, the sonne of Judah were Er the father of Lecah, and Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the householdes of them that wrought fine linen in the house of Ashbea.
4.22: And Jokim and the men of Chozeba and Joash, and Saraph, which had the dominion in Moab, and Iashubi Lehem. These also are auncient things.
4.23: These were potters, and dwelt among plants and hedges: there they dwelt with the king for his work.
4.24: The sonnes of Simeon were Nemuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul,
4.25: Whose sonne was Shallum, and his sonne, Mibsam, and his sonne Mishma.
4.26: And the sonnes of Mishma, Hamuel was his sonne, Zacchur his sonne, and Shimei his sonne.
4.27: And Shimei had sixteen sonnes, and six daughters, but his brethren had not many children, neither was all their familie like to the children of Judah in multitude.
4.28: And they dwelt at Beer-sheba, and at Moladah, and at Hazar Shual,
4.29: And at Bilhah, and at Ezem, and at Tolad,
4.30: And at Bethuel, and at Hormah, and at Ziklag,
4.31: And at Beth-marcaboth, and at Hazar Susim, at Beth-birei, and at Shaaraim, these were their cities unto the reign of David.
4.32: And their townes were Etam, and Ain, Rimmon, and Tochen, and Ashan, five cities.
4.33: And all their townes that were round about these cities unto Baal, These are their habitations and the declaration of their genealogie,
4.34: And Meshobab, and Jamlech, and Joshah the sonne of Amashiah,
4.35: And Joel and Jehu the sonne of Ioshibiah, the sonne of Seraiah, the sonne of Asiel,
4.36: And Elionai, and Jaakobah, and Jeshohaiah, and Asaiah, and Adiel, and Jesimiel, and Benaiah,
4.37: And Ziza the sonne of Shiphei, the sonne of Allon, the sonne of Jedaiah, the sonne of Shimri, the sonne of Shemaiah.
4.38: These were famous princes in their families, and increased greatly their fathers houses.
4.39: And they went to the entring in of Gedor, even unto the East side of the valley, to seek pasture for their sheep.
4.40: And they found fat pasture and good, and a wide land, both quiet and fruitful: for they of Ham had dwelt there before.
4.41: And these described by name, came in the dayes of Hezekiah king of Judah, and smote their tents, and the inhabitants that were found there, and destroyed them utterly unto this day, and dwelt in their roume, because there was pasture there for their sheep.
4.42: And besides these, five hundreth men of the sonnes of Simeon went to mount Seir, and Pelatiah, and Neariah, and Rophaiah, and Uzziel the sonnes of Ishi were their captaines,
4.43: And they smote the rest of Amalek that had escaped, and they dwelt there unto this day.

5.1: The sonnes also of Reuben the eldest sonne of Israel (for he was the eldest, but had defiled his fathers bed, therefore his birthright was given unto the sonnes of Joseph the sonne of Israel, so that the genealogie is not rekoned after his birthright.
5.2: For Judah prevailed above his brethren, and of him came the prince, but the birthright was Iosephs)
5.3: The sonnes of Reuben the eldest sonne of Israel, were Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.
5.4: The sonnes of Joel, Shemaiah his sonne, Gog his sonne, and Shimei his sonne,
5.5: Michah his sonne, Reaiah his sonne, and Baal his sonne,
5.6: Beerah his sonne: whom Tilgath Pilneeser King of Asshur caryed away: he was a prince of the Reubenites.
5.7: And when his brethren in their families rekoned the genealogie of their generations, Jeiel and Zechariah were the chief,
5.8: And Bela the sonne of Azaz, the sonne of Shema, the sonne of Joel, which dwelt in Aroer, even unto Nebo and Baal meon.
5.9: Also Eastward he inhabited unto the entring in of the wildernes from the river Perath for they had much cattel in the land of Gilead.
5.10: And in the dayes of Saul they warred with the Hagarims, which fell by their hands: and they dwelt in their tentes in all the East partes of Gilead.
5.11: And the children of Gad dwelt over against them in the land of Bashan, unto Salchah.
5.12: Joel was the chiefest, and Shapham the second, but Jaanai and Shaphat were in Bashan.
5.13: And their brethren of the house of their fathers were Michael, and Meshullam, and Sheba, and Sorai, and Iacan, and Zia and Eber, seven.
5.14: These are the childre of Abihail, the sonne of Huri, the sonne of Jaroah, the sonne of Gilead, the sonne of Michael, the sonne of Jeshishai, the sonne of Jahdo, the sonne of Buz.
5.15: Ahi the sonne of Abdiel, the sonne of Guni was chief of the houshold of their fathers.
5.16: And they dwelt in Gilead in Bashan, and in the townes thereof, and in all the suburbes of Sharon by their borders.
5.17: All these were rekoned by genealogies in the dayes of Jotham King of Judah, and in the dayes of Jeroboam King of Israel.
5.18: The sonnes of Reuben and of Gad, and of half the tribe of Manasseh of those that were viliant men, able to bear shield, and sword, and to draw a bow, exercised in war, were four and fourtie thousand, seven hundreth and three score, that went out to the war.
5.19: And they made war with the Hagarims, with Jetur, and Naphish, and Nodab.
5.20: And they were holpen against them, and the Hagarims were delivered into their hand, and all that were with them: for they cryed to God in the battel, and he heard them, because they trusted in him.
5.21: And they led away their cattel, even their camels fiftie thousand, and two hundreth, and fiftie thousand sheep, and two thousand asses, and of persons an hundreth thousand.
5.22: For many fel down wounded, because the war was of God. And they dwelt in their steads until the captiuitie.
5.23: And the children of the half tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land, from Baashan unto Baal Hermon, and Senir, and unto mount Hermon: for they increased.
5.24: And these were the heads of the housholds of their fathers, even Epher and Ishi, and Eliel and Azriel, and Jeremiah, and Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, strong men, valiant and famous, heades of the housholdes of their fathers.
5.25: But they transgressed against the God of their fathers, and went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.
5.26: And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Asshur, and the spirit of Tilgath Pilneeser king of Asshur, and he caryed them away: even the Reubenites and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, and brought them unto Halah and Habor, and Hara, and to the river Gozan, unto this day.

6.1: The sonnes of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
6.2: And the sonnes of Kohath, Amram, Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel.
6.3: And the children of Amram, Aaron, and Moses and Miriam. And the sonnes of Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and Eleazar, and Ithamar.
6.4: Eleazar begat Phinehas. Phinehas begat Abishua,
6.5: And Abishua begat Bukki, and Bukki begat Uzzi,
6.6: And Uzzi begat Zerahiah, and Zerahiah begat Meraioth.
6.7: Meraioth begat Amariah, and Amariah begat Ahitub,
6.8: And Ahitub begat Zadok, and Zadok begat Ahimaaz,
6.9: And Ahimaaz begat Azariah, and Azariah begat Johanan,
6.10: And Johanan begat Azariah (it was hee that was Priest in the house that Salomon built in Jerusalem)
6.11: And Azariah begat Amariah, and Amariah begat Ahitub,
6.12: And Ahitub begat Zadok, and Zadok begat Shallum,
6.13: And Shallum begat Hilkiah, and Hilkiah begat Azariah,
6.14: And Azariah begat Seraiah, and Seraiah begat Jehozadak,
6.15: And Jehozadak departed when the Lord caried away into captiuitie Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nebuchad-nezzar.
6.16: The sonnes of Levi were Gershom, Kohath and Merari.
6.17: And these be the names of the sonnes of Gershom, Libni, and Shimei.
6.18: And the sonnes of Kohath were Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron and Uzziel.
6.19: The sonnes of Merari, Mahli and Mushi: and these are the families of Levi concerning their fathers.
6.20: Of Gershom, Libni his sonne, Jahath his sonne, Zimmah his sonne,
6.21: Joah his sonne, Iddo his sonne, Zerah his sonne, Jeaterai his sonne.
6.22: The sonnes of Kohath, Aminadab his sonne, Korah his sonne, Assir his sonne,
6.23: Elkanah his sonne, and Ebiasaph his sonne, and Assir his sonne,
6.24: Tahath his sonne, Uriel his sonne, Uzziah his sonne, and Shaul his sonne,
6.25: And the sonnes of Elkanah, Amasai, and Ahimoth.
6.26: Elkanah. the sonnes of Elkanah, Zophai his sonne, and Nahath his sonne,
6.27: Eliab his sonne, Jeroham his sonne, Elkanah his sonne,
6.28: And the sonnes of Shemuel, the eldest Vashni, then Abiah.
6.29: The sonnes of Merari were Mahli, Libni his sonne, Shimei his sonne, Uzzah his sonne,
6.30: Shimea his sonne, Haggiah his sonne, Asaiah his sonne.
6.31: And these be they whom David set for to sing in the house of the Lord, after that the Ark had rest.
6.32: And they ministred before the Tabernacle, even the Tabernacle of the Congregation with singing, until Salomon had built ye house of the Lord in Jerusalem: then they continued in their office, according to their custom.
6.33: And these ministred with their children: of the sonnes of Kohath, Heman a singer, the sonne of Joel, the sonne of Shemuel,
6.34: The sonne of Elkanah, the sonne of Jeroham, the sonne of Eliel, the sonne of Toah,
6.35: The sonne of Zuph, the sonne of Elkanah, the sonne of Mahath, the sonne of Amasai,
6.36: The sonne of Elkanah, the sonne of Joel, the sonne of Azariah, the sonne of Zephaniah,
6.37: The sonne of Tahath, the sonne of Assir, the sonne of Ebiasaph, the sonne of Korah,
6.38: The sonne of Izhar, the sonne of Kohath, the sonne of Levi, the sonne of Israel.
6.39: And his brother Asaph stood on his right hand: and Asaph was the sonne of Berechiah, the sonne of Shimea,
6.40: The sonne of Michael, the sonne of Baaseiah, the sonne of Malchiah,
6.41: The sonne of Ethni, the sonne of Zerah, the sonne of Adaiah,
6.42: The sonne of Ethan, the sonne of Zimmah, the sonne of Shimei,
6.43: The sonne of Jahath, the sonne of Gershom, the sonne of Levi.
6.44: And their brethren the sonnes of Merari were on the left hand, even Ethan the sonne of Kishi, the sonne of Abdi, the sonne of Malluch,
6.45: The sonne of Hashabiah, the sonne of Amaziah, the sonne of Hilkiah,
6.46: The sonne of Amzi, the sonne of Bani, the sonne of Shamer,
6.47: The sonne of Mahli, the sonne of Mushi, the sonne of Merari, the sonne of Levi.
6.48: And their brethren the Levites were appointed unto all the service of the Tabernacle of the house of God,
6.49: But Aaron and his sonnes burnt incense upon the altar of burnt offering, and on the altar of incense, for all that was to do in the most holy place, and to make an atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.
6.50: These are also the sonnes of Aaron, Eleazar his sonne, Phinehas his sonne, Abishua his sonne,
6.51: Bukki his sonne, Uzzi his sonne, Zerahiah his sonne,
6.52: Meraioth his sonne, Amariah his sonne, Ahitub his sonne,
6.53: Zadok his sonne, and Ahimaaz his sonne.
6.54: And these are the dwelling places of them throughout their townes and coastes, even of the sonnes of Aaron for the familie of the Kohathites, for the lot was theirs.
6.55: So they gave them Hebron in the land of Judah and the suburbes thereof round about it.
6.56: But the field of the citie, and the villages thereof they gave to Caleb the sonne of Jephunneh.
6.57: And to the sonnes of Aaron they gave the cities of Judah for refuge, even Hebron and Libna with their suburbes, and Jattir, and Eshtemoa with their suburbes,
6.58: And Hilen with her suburbes, and Debir with her suburbes,
6.59: And Ashan and her suburbes, and Bethshemesh and her suburbes:
6.60: And of the tribe of Beniamin, Geba and her suburbes, and Alemeth with her suburbes, and Anathoth with her suburbes: all their cities were thirteen cities by their families.
6.61: And unto the sonnes of Kohath the remnant of the familie of the tribe, even of the half tribe of the half of Manasseh, by lot ten cities.
6.62: And to the sonnes of Gershom according to their families out of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
6.63: Unto the sonnes of Merari according to their families out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, by lot twelve cities.
6.64: Thus the children of Israel gave to the Levites cities with their suburbes.
6.65: And they gave by lot out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, and out of the tribe of the children of Beniamin, these cities, which they called by their names.
6.66: And they of the families of the sonnes of Kohath, had cities and their coastes out of the tribe of Ephraim.
6.67: And they gave unto them cities of refuge, Shechem in mount Ephraim, and her suburbes, and Gezer and her suburbes,
6.68: Jokmeam also and her suburbes, and Bethhoron with her suburbes,
6.69: And Aialon and her suburbes, and Gath Rimmon and her suburbes,
6.70: And out of the half tribe of Manasseh, Aner and her suburbes, and Bileam and her suburbes, for the families of the remnant of the sonnes of Kohath.
6.71: Unto the sonnes of Gershom out of the familie of the half tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan, and her suburbes, and Ashtaroth with her suburbes,
6.72: And out of the tribe of Issachar, Kedesh and her suburbes, Daberath and her suburbes,
6.73: Ramoth also and her suburbes, and Anem with her suburbes,
6.74: And out of the tribe of Asher, Mashal and her suburbes, and Abdon and her suburbes,
6.75: And Hukok and her suburbs, and Rehob and her suburbes,
6.76: And out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilea and her suburbes, and Hammon and her suburbes, and Kiriathaim and her suburbes.
6.77: Unto the rest of the children of Merari were given out of ye tribe of Zebulun Rimmon and her suburbes, Tabor and her suburbes,
6.78: And on the other side Iorden by Jericho, even on the Eastside of Iorden, out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer in the wilderness with her suburbes, and Jahzah with her suburbes,
6.79: And Kedemoth with her suburbes, and Mephaath with her suburbes,
6.80: And out of the tribe of Gad Ramoth in Gilead with her suburbes, and Mahanaim with her suburbes,
6.81: And Heshbon with her suburbes, and Jaazer with her suburbes.

7.1: And the sonnes of Issachar were Tola and Puah, Jashub, and Shimron, four,
7.2: And the sonnes of Tola, Uzzi, and Rephaiah, and Jeriel, and Jahmai, and Jibsam, and Shemuel, heads in the housholdes of their fathers. Of Tola were valiant men of war in their generations, whose nomber was in the dayes of David two and twentie thousand, and six hundreth.
7.3: And the sonne of Uzzi was Izrahaiah, and the sonnes of Izrahaiah, Michael, and Obadiah, and Joel, and Isshiah, five men all princes.
7.4: And with them in their generations after the houshold of their fathers were bandes of men of war for battel, six and thirtie thousand: for they had many wives and children.
7.5: And their brethren among all the families of Issachar were valiant men of war, rekoned in all by their genealogies four score and seven thousand.
7.6: The sonnes of Beniamin were Bela, and Becher, and Jediael, three.
7.7: And the sonnes of Bela, Ezbon, and Uzzi, and Uzziel, and Jerimoth, and Iri, five heads of the housholds of their fathers, valiant men of war, and were rekoned by their genealogies, two and twentie thousand and thirtie and four.
7.8: And the sonnes of Becher, Zemirah, and Joash, and Eliezer, and Elioenai, and Omri, and Jerimoth, and Abiah, and Anathoth, and Alameth: all these were the sonnes of Becher.
7.9: And they were nombred by their genealogies according to their generations, and the chief of the houses of their fathers, valiant men of war, twenty thousand and two hundreth.
7.10: And the sonne of Jediael was Bilhan, and the sonnes of Bilhan, Jeush, and Beniamin, and Ehud, and Chenaanah, and Zethan, and Tharshish, and Ahishahar.
7.11: All these were the sonnes of Jediael, chief of the fathers, valiant men of war, seventeen thousand and two hundreth, marching in battel aray to the war.
7.12: And Shuppim, and Huppim were ye sonnes of Ir, but Hushim was the sonne of another.
7.13: The sonnes of Naphtali, Jahziel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shallum of the sonnes of Bilhah.
7.14: The sonne of Manasseh was Ashriel whom she bare unto him, but his concubine of Aram bare Machir the father of Gilead.
7.15: And Machir took to wife the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, and the name of their sister was Maachah. And the name of the second sonne was Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had daughters.
7.16: And Maachah the wife of Machir bare a sonne, and called his name Peresh, and the name of his brother was Sheresh: and his sonnes were Ulam and Rakem.
7.17: And the sonne of Ulam was Bedan. These were the sonnes of Gilead the sonne of Machir, the sonne of Manasseh.
7.18: And his sister Molecheth bare Ishod, and Abiezer, and Mahalah.
7.19: And the sonnes of Shemida were Ahian, and Shechem, and Likhi, and Aniam.
7.20: The sonnes also of Ephraim were Shuthelah, and Bered his sonne, and Tahath his sonne, and his sonne Eladah, and Tahath his sonne,
7.21: And Zabad his sonne, and Shuthelah his sonne, and Ezer, and Elead: and the men of Gath that were borne in the land, slew them, because they came down to take away their cattel.
7.22: Therefore Ephraim their father mourned many dayes, and his brethren came to comfort him.
7.23: And when he went in to his wife, she conceived, and bare him a sonne, and he called his name Beriah, because affliction was in his house.
7.24: And his daughter was Sherah, which built Beth-horon the nether, and the upper, and Vzzen Sheerah.
7.25: And Rephah was his sonne, and Resheph, and Telah his sonne, and Tahan his sonne,
7.26: Laadan his sonne, Ammihud his sonne, Elishama his sonne,
7.27: Non his sonne, Jehoshua his sonne.
7.28: And their possessions and their habitations were Beth-el, and the villages thereof, and Eastward Naaran, and Westward Gezer with the villages thereof, Shechem also and the villages thereof, unto Azzah, and the villages thereof,
7.29: And by the places of the children of Manasseh, Beth-shean and her villages, Taanach and her villages, Megiddo and her villages, Dor and her villages. In those dwelt the children of Joseph the sonne of Israel.
7.30: The sonnes of Asher were Imnah, and Isuah, and Ishuai, and Beriah, and Serah their sister.
7.31: And the sonnes of Beriah, Heber, and Malchiel, which is the father of Birzavith.
7.32: And Heber begat Japhlet, and Shomer, and Hotham, and Shuah their sister.
7.33: And the sonnes of Japhlet were Pasach, and Bimhal, and Ashvath: these were the children of Japhlet.
7.34: And the sonnes of Shamer, Ahi, and Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
7.35: And the sonnes of his brother Helem were Zophah, and Jimna, and Shelesh and Amal.
7.36: The sonnes of Zophah, Suah, and Harnepher, and Shual, and Beri, and Imrah,
7.37: Bezer and Hod, and Shamma, and Shilshah, and Ithran, and Beera.
7.38: And the sonnes of Jether, Jephunneh, and Pispa and Ara.
7.39: And the sonnes of Ulla, Harah, and Haniel, and Rizia.
7.40: All these were the children of Asher, the heads of their fathers houses, noble men, valiant men of war and chief princes, and they were rekoned by their genealogies for war and for battell to the nomber of six and twentie thousand men.

8.1: Beniamin also begat Bela his eldest sonne, Ashbel the second, and Aharah the third,
8.2: Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fift.
8.3: And the sonnes of Bela were Addar, and Gera, and Abihud,
8.4: And Abishua, and Naaman and Ahoah,
8.5: And Gera, and Shephuphan, and Huram.
8.6: And these are the sonnes of Ehud: these were the chief fathers of those that inhabited Geba: and they were caryed away captives to Monahath,
8.7: And Naaman, and Ahiah, and Gera, he caryed them away captives: and he begat Uzza, and Ahihud.
8.8: And Shaharaim begat certain in the coutrey of Moab, after he had sent away Hushim and Baara his wives.
8.9: He begat, I say, of Hodesh his wife, Jobab and Zibia, and Mesha, and Malcham,
8.10: And Jeuz and Shachia and Mirma: these were his sonnes, and chief fathers.
8.11: And of Hushim he begat Ahitub and Elpaal.
8.12: And the sonnes of Elpaal were Eber, and Misham and Shamed (which built Ono, and Lod, and the villages thereof)
8.13: And Beriah and Shema (which were the chief fathers among the inhabitants of Aialon: they drave away the inhabitants of Gath)
8.15: And Sebadiah, and Arad, and Ader,
8.16: And Michael, and Ispah, and Joha, the sonnes of Beriah,
8.17: And Zebadiah, and Meshullam, and Hizki, and Heber,
8.18: And Ishmerai and Izliah, and Jobab, the sonnes of Elpaal,
8.19: Jakim also, and Zichri, and Sabdi,
8.20: And Elienai, and Zillethai, and Eliel,
8.21: And Adaiah, and Beraiah, and Shimrah the sonnes of Shimei,
8.22: And Ishpan, and Eber, and Eliel,
8.23: And Abdon, and Zichri, and Hanan,
8.24: And Hananiah, and Elam, and Antothiiah,
8.25: Iphedeiah and Penuel ye sonnes of Shashak,
8.26: And Shamsherai, and Shehariah, and Athaliah,
8.27: And Iaareshiah, and Eliah, and Zichri, the sonnes of Jeroham.
8.28: These were the chief fathers according to their generations, even princes, which dwelt in Jerusalem.
8.29: And at Gibeon dwelt the father of Gibeon, and the name of his wife was Maachah.
8.30: And his eldest sonne was Abdon, then Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Nadab,
8.31: And Gidor, and Ahio, and Zacher.
8.32: And Mikloth begat Shimeah: these also dwelt with their brethren in Jerusalem, even by their brethren.
8.33: And Ner begat Kish, and Kish begat Saul, and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
8.34: And the sonne of Jonathan was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal begat Micah.
8.35: And the sonnes of Micah were Pithon, and Melech, and Tarea, and Ahaz.
8.36: And Ahaz begat Jehoadah, and Jehoadah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri, and Zimri begat Moza,
8.37: And Moza begat Bineah, whose sonne was Raphah, and his sonne Eleasah, and his sonne Azel.
8.38: And Azel had six sonnes, whose names are these, Azrikam, Bocheru and Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan: all these were the sonnes of Azel.
8.39: And the sonnes of Eshek his brother were Ulam his eldest sonne, Jehush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
8.40: And the sonnes of Ulam were valiant men of war which shot with the bow, and had many sonnes and nephewes, an hundreth and fiftie: all these were of the sonnes of Beniamin.

9.1: Thus all Israel were nombred by their genealogies: and behold, they are written in the book of the Kings of Israel and of Judah, and they were caried away to Babel for their transgression.
9.2: And the chief inhabitants that dwelt in their own possessions, and in their own cities, even Israel the Priestes, the Levites, and the Nethinims.
9.3: And in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah, and of the children of Beniamin, and of the children of Ephraim, and Manasseh.
9.4: Uthai the sonne of Amihud the sonne of Omri, the sonne of Imri, the sonne of Bani: of the children of Pharez, the sonne of Judah.
9.5: And of Shiloni, Asaiah the eldest, and his sonnes.
9.6: And the sonnes of Zerah, Jeuel, and their brethren six hundreth and ninetie.
9.7: And of the sonnes of Beniamin, Sallu the sonne of Meshullam, the sonne of Hodaviah, the sonne of Hasenuah,
9.8: And Ibneiah the sonne of Jeroham, and Elah the sonne of Uzzi, the sonne of Michri, and Meshullam the sonne of Shephatiah, the sonne of Reuel, the sonne of Ibniiah.
9.9: And their brethren according to their generations nine hundreth, fiftie and six: all these men were chief fathers in the housholdes of their fathers.
9.10: And of the Priestes, Jedaiah, and Jehoiarib, and Jachin,
9.11: And Azariah the sonne of Hilkiah, ye sonne of Meshullam, the sonne of Zadok, the sonne of Meraioth, the sonne of Ahitub the chief of the house of God,
9.12: And Adaiah the sonne of Jeroham, ye sonne of Pashur, the sonne of Malchiiah, and Maasai the sonne of Adiel, the sonne of Jahzerah, the sonne of Meshullam, the sonne of Meshillemith, the sonne of Immer.
9.13: And their brethre the chief of the households of their fathers a thousand, seven hundreth and three score valiant men, for the work of the service of the house of God.
9.14: And of the Levites, Shemaiah the sonne of Hasshub, the sonne of Azrikam, the sonne of Hashabiah of the sonnes of Merari,
9.15: And Bakbakkar, Heresh and Galal, and Mattaniah the sonne of Micha, the sonne of Zichri, the sonne of Asaph,
9.16: And Obadiah the sonne of Shemaiah, the sonne of Galal, the sonne of Jeduthun, and Berechiah, the sonne of Asa, the sonne of Elkanah, that dwelt in the villages of the Netophathites.
9.17: And the porters were Shallum, and Akkub, and Talmon, and Ahiman, and their brethren: Shallum was the chief.
9.18: For they were porters to this time by companies of the children of Levi unto the Kinges gate eastward.
9.19: And Shallum the sonne of Kore the sonne of Ebiasaph the sonne of Korah, and his brethren the Korathites (of the house of their father) were over the work, and office to keep the gates of the Tabernacle: so their families were over the host of the Lord, keeping the entrie.
9.20: And Phinehas ye sonne of Eleazar was their guide, and the Lord was with him.
9.21: Zechariah the sonne of Meshelemiah was the porter of the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
9.22: All these were chosen for porters of the gates, two hundreth and twelve, which were nombred according to their genealogies by their townes. David established these and Samuel the Seer in their perpetual office.
9.23: So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of the house of the Lord, even of the house of the Tabernacle by wardes.
9.24: The porters were in four quarters Eastward, Westward, Northward and Southward.
9.25: And their brethren, which were in their townes, came at seven dayes from time to time with them.
9.26: For these four chief porters were in perpetual office, and were of the Levites and had charge of the chambers, and of the treasures in the house of God.
9.27: And they lay round about the house of God, because the charge was theirs, and they caused it to be opened every morning.
9.28: And certain of them had the rule of the ministring vessels: for they brought them in by tale, and brought them out by tale.
9.29: Some of them also were appoynted over the instruments, and over all the vessels of the Sanctuarie, and of the flour, and the wine, and the oyle, and the incense, and the sweet odours.
9.30: And certain of the sonnes of the Priestes made oyntments of sweet odours.
9.31: And Mattithiah one of the Levites which was the eldest sonne of Shallum the Korhite, had the charge of the things that were made in the frying panne.
9.32: And other of their brethren the sonnes of Kohath had the oversight of the shewbread to prepare it every Sabbath.
9.33: And these are the singers, the chief fathers of the Levites, which dwelt in the chambers, and had none other charge: for they had to do in that busines day and night:
9.34: These were the chief fathers of the Levites according to their generations, and the principal which dwelt at Jerusalem.
9.35: And in Gibeon dwelt ye father of Gibeon, Jeiel, and the name of his wife was Maachah.
9.36: And his eldest sonne was Abdon, then Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Ner, and Nadab,
9.37: And Gedor, and Ahio, and Zechariah, and Mikloth.
9.38: And Mikloth begat Shimeam: they also dwelt with their brethren at Jerusalem, even by their brethren.
9.39: And Ner begat Kish, and Kish begat Saul, and Saul begat Jonathan and Malchishua, and Abinadab and Eshbaal.
9.40: And the sonne of Jonathan was Merib-baal: and Merib-baal begat Micah.
9.41: And the sonnes of Micah were Pithon, and Melech and Tahrea.
9.42: And Ahaz begat Jarah, and Jarah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri, and Zimri begat Moza.
9.43: And Moza begat Binea, whose sonne was Rephaiah, and his sonne was Eleasah, and his sonne Azel.
9.44: And Azel had six sonnes, whose names are these, Azrikam, Bocheru, and Ismael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan: these are the sonnes of Azel.

10.1: Then the Philistims fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled before the Philistims, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa.
10.2: And the Philistims pursued after Saul and after his sonnes, and the Philistims smote Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua the sonnes of Saul.
10.3: And the battel was sore against Saul; and the archers hit him, and he was wounded of the archers.
10.4: Then sayde Saul to his armour bearer, Draw out thy sword, and thrust me thorowe therewith, lest these uncircumcised come and mock at me: but his armour bearer would not, for he was sore afraid: therefore Saul took the sword and fell upon it.
10.5: And when his armour bearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon the sword, and dyed.
10.6: So Saul dyed and his three sonnes, and all his house, they dyed together.
10.7: And when all the men of Israel that were in the valley, saw how they fledde, and that Saul and his sonnes were dead, they forsook their cities, and fled away, and the Philistims came, and dwelt in them.
10.8: And on the morrow when the Philistims came to spoyle them that were slain, they found Saul and his sonnes lying in mount Gilboa.
10.9: And when they had stript him, they took his head and his armour, and sent them into the land of the Philistims round about, to publish it unto their idoles, and to the people.
10.10: And they layd up his armour in the house of their god, and set up his head in the house of Dagon.
10.11: When all they of Jabesh Gilead heard all that the Philistims had done to Saul,
10.12: Then they arose (all the valiant men) and took the body of Saul, and the bodies of his sonnes, and brought them to Jabesh, and buryed the bones of them under an oke in Jabesh, and fasted seven dayes.
10.13: So Saul dyed for his transgression, that he committed against the Lord, even against the word of the Lord, which he kept not, and in that he sought and asked counsel of a familiar spirit,
10.14: And asked not of the Lord: therefore he slew him, and turned the kingdom unto David the sonne of Ishai.

11.1: Then all Israel gathered themselves to David unto Hebron, saying, Behold, we are thy bones and thy flesh.
11.2: And in time past, even when Saul was King, thou leddest Israel out and in: and the Lord thy God sayde unto thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be captain over my people Israel.
11.3: So came all the Elders of Israel to the King to Hebron, and David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the Lord. And they anoynted David King over Israel, according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Samuel.
11.4: And David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, which is Jebus, where were the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land.
11.5: And the inhabitants of Jebus said to David, Thou shalt not come in hither. Neuertheles David took the towre of Zion, which is the city of David.
11.6: And David sayd, Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites first, shalbe the chief and captain. So Joab the sonne of Zeruiah went first up, and was captain.
11.7: And David dwelt in the tower: therefore they called it the citie of David.
11.8: And he built the citie on every side, from Millo even round about, and Joab repaired the rest of the citie.
11.9: And David prospered, and grew: for the Lord of hostes was with him.
11.10: These also are the chief of the valiant men that were with David, and ioyned their force with him in his kingdom with al Israel, to make him King over Israel, according to the word of the Lord.
11.11: And this is the nomber of the valiant men whom David had, Jashobeam the sonne of Hachmoni, the chief among thirtie: he lift up his spear against three hundreth, whom he slew at one time.
11.12: And after him was Eleazar the sonne of Dodo the Ahohite, which was one of the three valiant men.
11.13: He was with David at Pas-dammim, and there the Philistims were gathered together to battel: and there was a parcel of ground full of barley, and the people fled before the Philistims.
11.14: And they stood in the middes of the field, and saved it, and slew the Philistims: so the Lord gave a great victorie.
11.15: And three of the thirtie captaines went to a rock to David, into the cave of Adullam. And the armie of the Philistims camped in the valley of Rephaim.
11.16: And when David was in the hold, the Philistims garison was at Beth-lehem.
11.17: And David longed, and said, Oh, that one would give me to drink of the water of the well of Beth-lehem that is at the gate.
11.18: Then these three brake thorowe the host of the Philistims, and drew water out of the well of Beth-lehem that was by the gate, and took it and brought it to David: but David would not drink of it, but powred it for an oblation to the Lord,
11.19: And said, Let not my God suffer me to do this: should I drink the blood of these mens lives? for they have brought it with the ieopardie of their lives: therefore he would not drink it: these things did these three mightie men.
11.20: And Abishai the brother of Joab, he was chief of the three, and he lift up his spear against three hundreth, and slew them, and had the name among the three.
11.21: Among the three he was more honourable then the two, and he was their captain: but he attained not unto the first three.
11.22: Benaiah the sonne of Jehoiada (the sonne of a valiant man) which had done many actes, and was of Kabzeel, he slew two strong men of Moab: he went down also and slew a lion in the middes of a pit in time of snow.
11.23: And he slew an Egyptian, a man of great stature, even five cubites long, and in the Egyptians hand was a spear like a weauers beam: and he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptians hand, and slew him with his own spear.
11.24: These things did Benaiah ye sonne of Jehoiada, and had the name among the three worthies.
11.25: Behold, he was honourable among thirtie, but he attained not unto the first three. And David made him of his counsel.
11.26: These also were valiant men of war, Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan the sonne of Dodo of Beth-lehem,
11.27: Shammoth the Harodite, Helez the Pelonite,
11.28: Ira the sonne of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Antothite,
11.29: Sibbecai the Husathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
11.30: Maharai the Netophathite, Heled ye sonne of Baanah the Netophathite,
11.31: Ithai the sonne of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Beniamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,
11.32: Hurai of the rivers of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,
11.33: Azmaveth the Baharumite, Elihaba the Shaalbonite,
11.34: The sonnes of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan the sonne of Shageh the Harite,
11.35: Ahiam the sonne of Sacar the Hararite, Eliphal the sonne of Ur,
11.36: Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahiiah the Pelonite,
11.37: Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai the sonne of Ezbai,
11.38: Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the sonne of Haggeri,
11.39: Zelek the Ammonite, Nahrai the Berothite, the armour bearer of Joab, the sonne of Zeruiah,
11.40: Ira the Ithrite, Garib the Ithrite,
11.41: Uriah the Hittite, Zabad the sonne of Ahlai,
11.42: Adina the sonne of Shiza the Reubenite, a captain of the Reubenites, and thirtie with him,
11.43: Hanan the sonne of Maachah, and Joshaphat the Mithnite,
11.44: Vzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sonnes of Otham the Aroerite,
11.45: Jediael the sonne of Shimri, and Joha his brother the Tizite,
11.46: Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai and Joshaviah the sonnes of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite,
11.47: Eliel and Obed, and Jaasiel the Mesobaite.

12.1: These also are they that came to David to Ziklag, while he was yet kept close, because of Saul the sonne of Kish: and they were among the valiant and helpers of the battel.
12.2: They were weaponed with bowes, and could use the right and the left hand with stones and with arrowes and with bowes, and were of Sauls brethren, even of Beniamin.
12.3: The chief were Ahiezer, and Joash the sonnes of Shemaah a Gibeathite, and Jeziel, and Pelet the sonnes of Asinaueth, Berachah and Jehu the Antothite,
12.4: And Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a valiant man among thirtie, and above the thirtie, and Jeremiah, and Iehaziel, and Johanan, and Ioshabad the Gederathite,
12.5: Eluzai, and Jerimoth, and Bealiah, and Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite,
12.6: Elkanah, and Ishiah, and Azariel, and Joezer, Jashobeam of Hakorehim,
12.7: And Joelah, and Zebadiah, the sonnes of Jeroham of Gedor,
12.8: And of the Gadites there separated them selves some unto David into the hold of the wilderness, valiant men of war, and men of armes, and apt for battel, which could handle spear and shield, and their faces were like the faces of lyons, and were like the roes in the mountaines in swiftnesse,
12.9: Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
12.10: Mishmanah the fourth, Jeremiah the fift,
12.11: Attai the sixt, Eliel the seventh,
12.12: Johanan the eight, Elzabad the ninth,
12.13: Jeremiah the tenth, Macbannai the eleventh.
12.14: These were the sonnes of Gad, captaines of the host: one of the least could resist an hundreth, and the greatest a thousand.
12.15: These are they that went over Iorden in the first moneth when he had filled over all his bankes, and put to flight all them of the valley, toward the East and the West.
12.16: And there came of the children of Beniamin, and Judah to the hold unto David,
12.17: And David went out to meet them, and answered and sayde unto them, If yee be come peaceably unto me to help me, mine heart shall be knit unto you, but if you come to betray me to mine adversaries, seeing there is no wickednes in mine handes, the God of our fathers behold it, and rebuke it.
12.18: And the spirit came upon Amasai, which was the chief of thirtie, and he said, Thine are we, David, and with thee, O sonne of Ishai. Peace, peace be unto thee, and peace be unto thine helpers: for thy God helpeth thee. Then David received them, and made them captaines of the garison.
12.19: And of Manasseh some fell to David, when he came with the Philistims against Saul to battell, but they helped them not: for the Princes of the Philistims by advisement sent him away, saying, He will fall to his master Saul for our heads.
12.20: As he went to Ziklag, there fell to him of Manasseh, Adnah, and Jozabad, and Jediael, and Michael, and Jozabad, and Elihu, and Ziltai, heads of the thousands that were of Manasseh.
12.21: And they helped David against that bad: for they were all valiant men and were captaines in the host.
12.22: For at that time day by day there came to David to help him, until it was a great host, like the host of God.
12.23: And these are the nombers of the captaines that were armed to battell, and came to David to Hebron to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the word of the Lord.
12.24: The children of Judah that bare shield and spear, were six thousand and eight hundreth armed to the war.
12.25: Of the children of Simeon valiant men of war, seven thousand and an hundreth.
12.26: Of the children of Levi four thousand and six hundreth.
12.27: And Jehoiada was the chief of them of Aaron: and with him three thousand and seven hundreth.
12.28: And Zadok a yong man very valiant, and of his fathers housholde came two and twentie captaines.
12.29: And of the children of Beniamin the brethren of Saul three thousand: for a great part of them unto that time kept the ward of the house of Saul.
12.30: And of the children of Ephraim twentie thousand, and eight hundreth valiant men and famous men in the housholde of their fathers.
12.31: And of the half tribe of Manasseh eighteen thousand, which were appointed by name to come and make David King.
12.32: And of the children of Issachar which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to doe: the heades of them were two hundreth, and all their brethren were at their commandement.
12.33: Of Zebulun that went out to battel, expert in war, and in all instruments of war, fiftie thousand which could set the battell in aray: they were not of a double heart.
12.34: And of Naphtali a thousand captaines, and with them with shield and spear seven and thirtie thousand.
12.35: And of Dan expert in battell, eyght and twentie thousand, and six hundreth.
12.36: And of Asher that went out to the battell and were trained in the wars, fourtie thousand.
12.37: And of the other side of Iorden of the Reubenites, and of the Gadites, and of the half tribe of Manasseh with all instruments of war to fight with, an hundreth and twentie thousand.
12.38: All these men of war that could lead an armie, came with upright heart to Hebron to make David King over all Israel: and all the rest of Israel was of one accord to make David King:
12.39: And there they were with David three dayes, eating and drinking: for their brethren had prepared for them.
12.40: Moreover they that were neere them until Issachar, and Zebulun, and Naphtali brought bread upon asses, and on camels, and on mules, and on oxen, even meat, flour, figges, and reisins, and wine and oyle, and beeves and sheep abundantly: for there was joy in Israel.

13.1: And David counselled with the captaines of thousandes and of hundreths, and with all the gouernours.
13.2: And David said to all the Congregation of Israel, If it seem good to you, and that it proceedeth of the Lord our God, we will send to and from unto our brethren, that are left in all the land of Israel (for with them are the Priests and the Levites in the cities and their suburbes) that they may assemble them selves unto us.
13.3: And we will bring again the Ark of our God to us: for we sought not unto it in the dayes of Saul.
13.4: And all the Congregation answered, Let us doe so: for the thing seemed good in the eyes of all the people.
13.5: So David gathered all Israel together from Shihor in Egypt, even unto the entring of Hamath, to bring the Ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.
13.6: And David went up and all Israel to Baalath, in Kiriath-jearim, that was in Judah, to bring up from thence the Ark of God the Lord that dwelleth between the Cherubims, where his Name is called on.
13.7: And they caryed the Ark of God in a new cart out of the house of Abinadab: and Uzza and Ahio guided the cart.
13.8: And David and all Israel played before God with all their might, both with songes and with harpes, and with violes, and with timbrels and with cymbales and with trumpets.
13.9: And when they came unto the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzza put forth his hand to hold the Ark, for the oxen did shake it.
13.10: But the wrath of the Lord was kindled against Uzza, and he smote him, because he layed his hand upon the Ark: so he dyed there before God.
13.11: And David was angrie, because the Lord had made a breach in Uzza, and he called the name of that place Perez-uzza unto this day.
13.12: And David feared God that day, saying, How shall I bring in to me the Ark of God?
13.13: Therefore David brought not the Ark to him into the citie of David, but caused it to turn into the house of Obed Edom the Gittite.
13.14: So the Ark of God remained in the house of Obed Edom, even in his house three moneths: and the Lord blessed the house of Obed Edom, and all that he had.

14.1: Then sent Hiram the King of Tyrus messengers to David, and cedar trees, with masons and carpenters to build him an house.
14.2: Therefore David knew that the Lord had confirmed him King over Israel, and that his kingdom was lift up on hie, because of his people Israel.
14.3: Also David took moe wives at Jerusalem, and David begat moe sonnes and daughters.
14.4: And these are the names of the children which he had at Jerusalem, Shammua, and Shobab, Nathan, and Salomon,
14.5: And Ibhar, and Elishua, and Elpalet,
14.6: And Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
14.7: And Elishama, and Beeliada, and Eliphalet.
14.8: But when the Philistims heard that David was anointed King over Israel, all the Philistims came up to seek David. And when David heard, he went out against them.
14.9: And the Philistims came, and spred them selves in the valley of Rephaim.
14.10: Then David asked counsel at God, saying, Shall I goe up against the Philistims, and wilt thou deliver them into mine hand? And the Lord said unto him, Goe up: for I will deliver them into thine hand.
14.11: So they came up to Baal-perazim, and David smote them there: and David said, God hath deuided mine enemies with mine hand, as waters are deuided: therefore they called the name of that place, Baal-perazim.
14.12: And there they had left their gods: and David said, Let them even be burnt with fire.
14.13: Again the Philistims came and spread them selves in the valley.
14.14: And when David asked again counsel at God, God said to him, Thou shalt not goe up after them, but turn away from them, that thou mayest come upon them over against the mulberie trees.
14.15: And when thou hearest the noyse of one going in the toppes of the mulberie trees, then goe out to battel: for God is gone foorth before thee, to smite the host of the Philistims.
14.16: So David did as God had commanded him: and they smote the host of the Philistims from Gibeon even to Gezer.
14.17: And the fame of David went out into all landes, and the Lord brought the fear of him upon all nations.

15.1: And David made him houses in the citie of David, and prepared a place for the Ark of God, and pitched for it a tent.
15.2: Then David said, None ought to carie the Ark of God, but the Levites: for the Lord hath chosen them to bear the Ark of the Lord, and to minister unto him for ever.
15.3: And David gathered all Israel together to Jerusalem to bring up the Ark of the Lord unto his place, which he had ordeined for it.
15.4: And David assembled the sonnes of Aaron, and the Levites.
15.5: Of the sonnes of Kohath, Uriel the chief, and his brethren six score.
15.6: Of the sonnes of Merari, Asaiah the chief, and his brethren two hundreth and twentie.
15.7: Of the sonnes of Gershom, Joel the chief, and his brethren an hundreth and thirtie.
15.8: Of the sonnes of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, and his brethren two hundreth.
15.9: Of the sonnes of Hebron, Eliel the chief, and his brethren fourescore.
15.10: Of the sonnes of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, and his brethren an hundreth and twelve.
15.11: And David called Zadok and Abiathar the Priestes, and of the Levites, Uriel, Asaiah and Joel, Shemaiah, and Eliel, and Amminadab:
15.12: And he said unto them, Ye are the chief fathers of the Levites: sanctifie your selves, and your brethren, and bring up the Ark of the Lord God of Israel unto the place that I have prepared for it.
15.13: For because ye were not there at the first, the Lord our God made a breach among us: for we sought him not after due order.
15.14: So the Priestes and the Levites sanctified them selves to bring up the Ark of the Lord God of Israel.
15.15: And the sonnes of the Levites bare the Ark of God upon their shoulders with the barres, as Moses had commanded, according to the word of the Lord.
15.16: And David spake to the chief of the Levites, that they should appoint certain of their brethren to sing with instruments of musike, with violes and harpes, and cymbales, that they might make a sound, and lift up their voyce with ioye.
15.17: So the Levites appointed Heman the sonne of Joel, and of his brethren Asaph the sonne of Berechiah, and of the sonnes of Merari their brethren, Ethan the sonne of Kushaiah,
15.18: And with them their brethren in the second degree, Zechariah, Ben, and Jaaziel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Unni, Eliab, and Benaiah, and Maaseiah, and Mattithiah, and Elipheleh, and Mikneah, and Obed Edom, and Jeiel the porters.
15.19: So Heman, Asaph and Ethan were fingers to make a sound with cymbales of brass,
15.20: And Zechariah, and Aziel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Unni, and Eliab, and Maaseiah, and Benaiah with violes on Alamoth,
15.21: And Mattithiah, and Elipheleh, and Mikneah, and Obed Edom, and Jeiel, and Azaziah, with harpes upon Sheminith Ienazzeah.
15.22: But Chenaniah the chief of the Levites had the charge, bearing ye burden in the charge, for he was able to instruct.
15.23: And Berechiah and Elkanah were porters for the Ark.
15.24: And Shecaniah and Jehoshaphat and Nethaneel and Amasai, and Zechariah, and Benaiah, and Eliezer the Priestes did blow with trumpets before the Ark of God, and Obed Edom and Ieiiah were porters for the Ark.
15.25: So David and the Elders of Israel and the captaines of thousandes went to bring up the Ark of the covenant of the Lord from the house of Obed Edom with ioye.
15.26: And because that God helped the Levites that bare the Ark of the covenant of the Lord, they offered seven bullockes and seven rammes.
15.27: And David had on him a linen garment, as all the Levites that bare the Ark, and the singers and Chenaniah that had the chief charge of the singers: and upon David was a linen Ephod.
15.28: Thus all Israel brought up the Ark of the Lordes covenant with shouting and sound of cornet, and with trumpets, and with cymbales, making a sound with violes and with harpes.
15.29: And when the Ark of the covenant of the Lord came into the citie of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at a window, and saw King David dauncing and playing, and she despised him in her heart.

16.1: So they brought in the Ark of God, and set it in the middes of the Tabernacle that David had pitched for it, and they offred burnt offrings and peace offrings before God.
16.2: And when David had made an end of offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, hee blessed the people in the Name of the Lord.
16.3: And he dealt to every one of Israel both man and woman, to every one a cake of bread, and a piece of flesh, and a bottel of wine.
16.4: And he appointed certain of the Levites to minister before the Ark of the Lord, and to rehearse and to thank and prayse the Lord God of Israel:
16.5: Asaph the chief, and next to him Zechariah, Jeiel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Mattithiah, and Eliab, and Benaiah, and Obed Edom, even Jeiel with instruments, violes and harpes, and Asaph to make a sound with cymbales,
16.6: And Benaiah and Jahaziel Priestes, with trumpets continually before the Ark of the covenant of God.
16.7: Then at that time David did appoint at the beginning to give thankes to the Lord by the hand of Asaph and his brethren.
16.8: Praise the Lord and call upon his Name: declare his workes among the people.
16.9: Sing unto him, sing praise unto him, and talk of all his wonderful workes.
16.10: Reioyce in his holy Name: let the hearts of them that seek the Lord reioyce.
16.11: Seek the Lord and his strength: seek his face continually.
16.12: Remember his marueilous workes that he hath done, his wonders, and the iudgements of his mouth,
16.13: O seed of Israel his servant, O the children of Iaakob his chosen.
16.14: He is the Lord our God: his iudgements are throughout all the earth.
16.15: Remember his covenant for ever, and the word, which hee commanded to a thousand generations:
16.16: Which he made with Abraham, and his othe to Izhak:
16.17: And hath confirmed it to Iaakob for a Law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant,
16.18: Saying, To thee will I give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance.
16.19: When ye were few in number, yea, a very few, and strangers therein,
16.20: And walked about from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people,
16.21: He suffered no man to do them wrong, but rebuked Kings for their sakes, saying,
16.22: Touch not mine anoynted, and doe my Prophets no harm.
16.23: Sing unto the Lord all the earth: declare his salvation from day to day.
16.24: Declare his glory among the nations, and his wonderful workes among all people.
16.25: For the Lord is great and much to be praised, and hee is to bee feared above all gods.
16.26: For all the gods of the people are idoles, but the Lord made the heavens.
16.27: Prayse and glory are before him: power and beautie are in his place.
16.28: Give unto the Lord, ye families of the people: give unto the Lord glory and power.
16.29: Give unto the Lord ye glory of his Name: bring an offring and come before him, and worship the Lord in the glorious Sanctuarie.
16.30: Tremble ye before him, al the earth: surely the world shalbe stable and not move.
16.31: Let the heavens reioyce, and let the earth be glad, and let them say among the nations, The Lord reigneth.
16.32: Let the sea roar, and all that therein is: Let the field be ioyfull and all that is in it.
16.33: Let the trees of the wood then reioyce at the presence of the Lord: for he cometh to judge the earth.
16.34: Prayse the Lord, for hee is good, for his mercie endureth for ever.
16.35: And say ye, Save us, O God, our salvation, and gather us, and deliver us from the heathen, that we may prayse thine holy Name, and glorie in thy praise.
16.36: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel for ever and ever: and let all people say, So be it, and praise the Lord.
16.37: Then he left there before the Ark of the Lordes covenant Asaph and his brethren to minister continually before the Ark, that which was to be done every day:
16.38: And Obed Edom and his brethren, three score and eight: and Obed Edom the sonne of Jeduthun, and Hosah were porters.
16.39: And Zadok the Priest and his brethren the Priestes were before the Tabernacle of ye Lord, in the hie place that was at Gibeon,
16.40: To offer burnt offrings unto the Lord, upon the burnt offring altar continually, in the morning and in the evening, even according unto all that is written in the law of the Lord, which hee commanded Israel.
16.41: And with them were Heman, and Jeduthun, and the rest that were chosen (which were appointed by names) to praise the Lord, because his mercie endureth for ever.
16.42: Even with them were Heman and Ioduthun, to make a sound with the cornets and with the cymbales, with excellent instruments of musick: and the sonnes of Jeduthun were at the gate.
16.43: And all the people departed, euerie man to his house: and David returned to bless his house.

17.1: Now afterward when David dwelt in his house, he said to Nathan the Prophet, Behold, I dwell in an house of cedar trees, but the Ark of the Lordes covenant remaineth under curtaines.
17.2: Then Nathan said to David, Do all that is in thine heart: for God is with thee.
17.3: And the same night even the word of God came to Nathan, saying,
17.4: Goe, and tell David my servant, Thus saith the Lord, Thou shalt not buylde me an house to dwell in:
17.5: For I have dwelt in no house, since the day that I brought out the childre of Israel unto this day, but I have been from tent to tent, and from habitation to habitation.
17.6: Wheresoever I have walked with all Israel spake I one word to any of the judges of Israel (whom I commanded to feed my people) saying, Why have ye not built mee an house of cedar trees?
17.7: Now therefore thus shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith the Lord of hostes, I took thee from the sheepecoat and from following the sheep, that thou shouldest bee a prince over my people Israel.
17.8: And I have been with thee whithersoever thou hast walked, and have destroyed all thine enemies out of thy sight, and have made thee a name, like the name of the great men that are in the earth.
17.9: (Also I will appoynt a place for my people Israel, and will plant it, that they may dwell in their place, and move no more: neither shall the wicked people vex them any more, as at the beginning,
17.10: And since the time that I commanded judges over my people Israel) And I wil subdue all thine enemies: therefore I say unto thee, that the Lord wil buylde thee an house.
17.11: And when thy dayes shalbe fulfilled to go with thy fathers, then will I rayse up thy seed after thee, which shalbe of thy sonnes, and will stablish his kingdom.
17.12: He shall build me an house, and I will stablish his throne for ever.
17.13: I wil be his father, and he shalbe my sonne, aud I will not take my mercie away from him, as I took it from him that was before thee.
17.14: But I wil establish him in mine house, and in my kingdom for ever, and his throne shalbe stablished for ever,
17.15: According to all these wordes, and according to al this vision. So Nathan spake to David.
17.16: And David the King went in and sat before the Lord and said, Who am I, O Lord God, and what is mine house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?
17.17: Yet thou esteeming this a small thing, O God, hast also spoken concerning the house of thy seruaut for a great while, and hast regarded me according to the estate of a man of hie degree, O Lord God.
17.18: What can David desire more of thee for the honour of thy servant? for thou knowest thy servant.
17.19: O Lord, for thy seruantes sake, even according to thine heart hast thou done all this great thing to declare all magnificence.
17.20: Lord, there is none like thee, neither is there any God besides thee, according to all that we have heard with our eares.
17.21: Moreover what one nation in the earth is like thy people Israel, whose God went to redeem them to be his people, and to make thy self a Name, and to doe great and terrible things by casting out nations from before thy people, whom thou hast delivered out of Egypt?
17.22: For thou hast ordeined thy people Israel to be thine own people for ever, and thou Lord art become their God.
17.23: Therefore now Lord, let the thing that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant and concerning his house, be confirmed for ever, and doe as thou hast sayd,
17.24: And let thy name be stable and magnified for ever, that it may be sayd, The Lord of hostes, God of Israel, is the God of Israel, and let the house of David thy servant bee stablished before thee.
17.25: For thou, O my God, hast reueiled unto the ear of thy servant, that thou wilt build him an house: therefore thy servant hath been bold to pray before thee.
17.26: Therefore now Lord (for thou art God, and hast spoken this goodness unto thy servant)
17.27: Now therfore, it hath pleased thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may bee before thee for ever: for thou, O Lord, hast blessed it, and it shalbe blessed for ever.

18.1: And after this David smote the Philistims, and subdued them, and took Gath, and the villages thereof out of the hand of the Philistims.
18.2: And he smote Moab, and the Moabites became Dauids servants, and brought giftes.
18.3: And David smote Hadarezer King of Zobah unto Hamath, as he went to stablish his border by the river Perath.
18.4: And David took from him a thousand charets, and seven thousand horsemen, and twentie thousand footemen, and destroyed all the charets, but he reserved of them an hundreth charets.
18.5: Then came the Aramites of Damascus to succour Hadarezer King of Zobah, but David slew of the Aramites two and twentie thousand.
18.6: And David put a garison in Aram of Damascus, and the Aramites became Dauids servants, and brought giftes: and the Lord preserved David wheresoever he went.
18.7: And David took the shieldes of gold that were of the servants of Hadarezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
18.8: And from Tibhath, and from Chun (cities of Hadarezer) brought David exceeding much brass, wherewith Salomon made the brasen Sea, and the pillars and the vessels of brass.
18.9: Then Tou King of Hamath heard how David had smitten all the host of Hadarezer King of Zobah:
18.10: Therefore he sent Hadoram his sonne to King David, to salute him, and to reioyce with him, because he had fought against Hadarezer, and beaten him (for Tou had war with Hadarezer) who brought all vessels of gold and silver and brass.
18.11: And King David did dedicate them unto the Lord, with the silver and gold that hee brought from all the nations, from Edom, and from Moab, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistims, and from Amalek.
18.12: And Abishai the sonne of Zeruiah smote of Edom in the salt valley eighteen thousand,
18.13: And he put a garison in Edom, and all the Edomites became Dauids seruantes: and the Lord preserved David wheresoever he went.
18.14: So David reigned over all Israel, and executed iudgement and justice to all his people.
18.15: And Joab the sonne of Zeruiah was over the host, and Jehoshaphat the sonne of Ahilud recorder,
18.16: And Zadok the sonne of Ahitub, and Abimelech the sonne of Abiathar were the Priests, and Shavsha the Scribe,
18.17: And Benaiah the sonne of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites: and the sonnes of David were chief about the King.

19.1: After this also Nahash the King of the children of Ammon dyed, and his sonne reigned in his stead.
19.2: And David said, I will shew kindness unto Hanun the sonne of Nahash, because his father shewed kindness unto me. And David sent messengers to comfort him for his father. So the servants of David came into the land of the children of Ammon to Hanun to comfort him.
19.3: And the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun, Thinkest thou that David doeth honour thy father, that he hath sent comforters unto thee? Are not his servants come to thee to search, to seek and to spie out the land?
19.4: Wherefore Hanun took Dauids servants, and shaved them, and cut off their garments by the half unto the buttocks, and sent them away.
19.5: And there went certain and told David concerning the men: and he sent to meet them (for the men were exceedingly ashamed) and the King said, Tarie at Jericho, until your beardes be growen: then return.
19.6: When the children of Ammon saw that they stank in the sight of David, then sent Hanun and the children of Ammon a thousand talents of silver to hire them charets and horsemen out of Aram Naharaim and out of Aram Maachah, and out of Zobah.
19.7: And they hired them two and thirty thousand charets, and the King of Maachah and his people, which came and pitched before Medeba: and the children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to the battell.
19.8: And when David heard, he sent Joab and all the host of the valiant men.
19.9: And the children of Ammon came out, and set their battell in aray at the gate of the citie. And the Kings that were come, were by them selves in the field.
19.10: When Joab saw that the front of the battel was against him before and behind, then he chose out of all the choyse of Israel, and set him self in aray to meet the Aramites.
19.11: And the rest of the people he delivered unto the hand of Abishai his brother, and they put them selves in aray against the children of Ammon.
19.12: And he said, If Aram be too strong for me, then thou shalt succour me: and if the children of Ammon prevail against thee, then I wil succour thee.
19.13: Be strong, and let us shew our selves valiant for our people, and for the cities of our God, and let the Lord doe that which is good in his own sight.
19.14: So Joab and the people that was with him, came neere before the Aramites unto the battel, and they fled before him.
19.15: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Aramites fled, they fled also before Abishai his brother, and entred into the citie: so Joab came to Jerusalem.
19.16: And when the Aramites saw that they were discomfited before Israel, they sent messengers and caused the Aramites to come forth that were beyond the river: and Shophach the captain of the host of Hadarezer went before them.
19.17: And when it was shewed David, he gathered all Israel, and went over Iorden, and came unto them, and put him self in aray against them: And when David had put him self in battel aray to meet the Aramites, they fought with him.
19.18: But the Aramites fled before Israel, and David destroyed of the Aramites seven thousand charets, and fourtie thousand footemen, and killed Shophach the captain of the host.
19.19: And when the servants of Hadarezer saw that they fell before Israel, they made peace with David, and served him. And the Aramites would no more succour the children of Ammon.

20.1: And when the yere was expired, in the time that Kings goe out a warfare, Joab caryed out the strength of the armie, and destroyed the countrey of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah (but David taryed at Jerusalem) and Joab smote Rabbah and destroyed it.
20.2: Then David took the crown of their King from off his head, and found it the weight of a talent of gold, with precious stones in it: and it was set on Dauids head, and he brought away the spoyle of the citie exceeding much.
20.3: And he caryed away the people that were in it, and cut them with sawes, and with harowes of yron, and with axes: even thus did David with all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people came again to Jerusalem.
20.4: And after this also there arose war at Gezer with the Philistims: then Sibbechai the Hushathite slew Sippai, of the children of Haraphah, and they were subdued.
20.5: And there was yet another battell with the Philistims: and Elhanan the sonne of Jair slew Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite, whose spearestaffe was like a weauers beam.
20.6: And yet again there was a battel at Gath, where was a man of a great stature, and his fingers were by sixes, even four and twentie, and was also the sonne of Haraphah.
20.7: And when he reviled Israel, Jehonathan the sonne of Shimea Dauids brother did slay him.
20.8: These were borne unto Haraphah at Gath, and fell by the hand of David: and by the hands of his servants.

21.1: And Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to nomber Israel.
21.2: Therefore David said to Joab, and to the rulers of the people, Go, and nomber Israel from Beer-sheba even to Dan, and bring it to me, that I may know the nomber of them.
21.3: And Joab answered, The Lord increase his people an hundreth times so many as they be, O my lord the King: are they not all my lords seruats? wherefore doeth my lord require this thing? why should he be a cause of trespass to Israel?
